inline_comments.comment:
Listing `'stress'` in `implemented_properties` while conditionally not setting it in `self.results` relies on an implicit fallback in `Calculator.get_property()`: after `calculate()` returns without setting `'stress'`, the post-call check at line 522 of `calculator.py` raises `PropertyNotImplementedError`. This works, but it is fragile and misleading — `implemented_properties` is an unconditional advertisement of capabilities, so users who check `'stress' in calc.implemented_properties` will incorrectly conclude stress is always available.

Follow the explicit pattern used in EMT:
```python
if self.atoms.cell.rank == 3:
    self.results['stress'] = stress
elif 'stress' in properties:
    raise PropertyNotImplementedError(
        'stress requires a full 3D cell'
    )
```
This matches the project-standard approach and makes the contract clear without relying on the implicit fallback.

`free_energy` is set equal to the biased total energy with no explanation. In ASE, `free_energy` typically has DFT-specific semantics (the Helmholtz free energy of the electronic system, used by `get_potential_energy(force_consistent=True)`).

Add a short inline comment explaining the rationale, e.g.:
```python
# free_energy = biased energy; allows force_consistent=True in thermostats
self.results['free_energy'] = float(energy)
```

`except Exception` is far too broad. If the inner calculator raises a `RuntimeError`, `AttributeError`, or any other genuine programming error, it will be silently swallowed and replaced with `np.zeros(6)` — masking a real bug as a quietly wrong zero-stress result.

Catch only the expected case:
```python
from ase.calculators.calculator import PropertyNotImplementedError
...
except PropertyNotImplementedError:
    unbiased_stress = np.zeros(6)
```

There is no comment explaining why `virial_bias / volume` is correct without a sign flip. A future maintainer seeing a raw division might "fix" it by adding a negation, breaking the result.

PLUMED fills `virial_bias` as `W_αβ = Σ_i r_i_α · (∂U/∂r_i)_β`, i.e. negative-force × position. ASE's stress convention (see EMT: `stress -= outer(r, f)`) is also `σ_αβ = −Σ_i r_i_α · f_i_β / V = W_αβ / V`. Add an inline comment, e.g.:
```python
# PLUMED virial W_αβ = Σ r_α · (∂U/∂r)_β; matches ASE sign convention (stress = W/V)
biased_stress_voigt = full_3x3_to_voigt_6_stress(virial_bias) / volume
```

The two new imports are appended after the existing `ase.calculators.*` imports rather than sorted into the correct alphabetical position. `ase.calculators.calculator` and `ase.calculators.fd` both precede `ase.calculators.lj` alphabetically. They should be placed before `from ase.calculators.lj import LennardJones` to comply with project import ordering (enforced by `ruff`).

Trailing whitespace after the trailing comma on the split `Atoms(...)` constructor line. The same issue appears on the blank line immediately below (line 292). Ruff/flake8 will flag these. The same pattern recurs in `test_forces_and_stress` at approximately lines 314 and 316.

Two issues:
1. The file is missing a trailing newline (indicated by `\ No newline at end of file`). RST scriv fragments must end with a newline.
2. The entry references the calculator only by file path. Per project conventions, use a Sphinx `:class:` cross-reference: `:class:`~ase.calculators.plumed.Plumed``. Also, per changelog guidelines, double-check whether the implicit energy scalar fix (see general comments) merits a separate bullet under `Bugfixes`.

general_comments.comment: `self.calc.get_stress(self.atoms)` is now called unconditionally inside `compute_energy_and_forces` for every 3D-cell calculation, even when `properties` does not include `'stress'` (e.g., a pure NVE run). For calculators that cache results after `get_potential_energy` + `get_forces`, this is free. But for calculators that do not (or where stress is computed by a separate, expensive call), every energy/force evaluation now silently incurs the additional cost of a stress calculation. Guard the call with `if 'stress' in properties:`, passing `properties` down from `calculate()` to `compute_energy_and_forces()`.

This MR silently fixes a pre-existing bug: the old code returned `energy_bias` as a numpy array of shape `(1,)` from `compute_bias`, which meant `self.results['energy']` was stored as a `(1,)` array instead of a scalar. The fix — `energy_bias = energy_bias[0]` in `compute_bias` plus `float(energy)` in `calculate` — is correct and welcome, but it is an unremarked behavior change. The changelog entry should call this out explicitly so downstream users who may have been relying on the `(1,)` shape (e.g., by indexing `calc.results['energy'][0]`) are aware.
